messages:
lina_sales: quick heads up - POC customer on managed enterprise network hitting SSL errors from both our TS SDK and their internal Python service. they said it works from home but not from office.

ben_se: what do the errors look like?

lina_sales: provided two snippets:
- node: `error: certificate has expired` then `write EPROTO`
- python: `ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate`

mike_eng: looks like their corp proxy is resigning certs. probably not trusting our CA chain or they have custom root. could also be older OpenSSL on their python env.

tara_sre: confirm whether they use explicit HTTP proxy or transparent interception. if explicit, tunneling (CONNECT) should preserve certs. if interception, they'll see our cert replaced.

lina_sales: asked customer - they use "CorpGate" outbound proxy that performs SSL inspection and uses a company root CA. they cannot install our CA.

ben_se: two options: 1) they import corp root into their runtimes (node/pip/cert store) OR 2) we provide a dedicated POC hostname/IP that they can whitelist and route via passthrough so TLS stays end-to-end.

mike_eng: for node, if their proxy allows CONNECT, use `https-proxy-agent` so TLS is end-to-end. if proxy always intercepts, need root import. sample: `const agent = new HttpsProxyAgent(process.env.HTTPS_PROXY)` then fetch with agent.

ben_se: python guidance: if using `requests`, set `session.verify` to path of system bundle that includes corp CA, or for macOS dev env use `Install Certificates.command` for python. but in corp infra they must add corp CA to the system store so python ssl trusts it.

lina_sales: customer asks if we can force TLSv1.3 or change headers to avoid inspection.

tara_sre: we only support TLS 1.2+ and can't change their proxy behavior. forcing TLSv1.3 won't stop inspection if they terminate TLS. SNI must be preserved for virtual hosts. if their proxy strips SNI, the handshake will fail.

ops-bot: infra task created: RED-POC-739 to provision temporary hostname for POC whitelist. assigned to mike_eng.

mike_eng: provisioning `poc-enterprise-739.api.redwood.ai`. will provide IPs and certs once ready. expect ~2 hours.

lina_sales: great. can you also share a short checklist for their network team?

ben_se: checklist to send: 1) confirm proxy type (explicit vs transparent) and whether CONNECT is allowed; 2) try `curl --proxy http://proxy:8080 -v https://api.redwood.ai` to check for CONNECT behavior; 3) if interception/resigning occurs and they can't import CA, request passthrough for `poc-enterprise-739.api.redwood.ai` or allow the IP CIDR; 4) update Node/Python trust stores if they choose to accept corp CA; 5) set SDK timeouts to 30s and enable retries with exponential backoff to avoid failing fast on intermittent proxy errors.

lina_sales: sent checklist. customer says proxy team needs IPs. mike - pls share when ready.

mike_eng: IPs: 34.210.45.98, 34.210.45.99, 34.210.45.100. cert provisioning done.

lina_sales: sent IPs to customer. they whitelisted and tested. node app works immediately; python service needed cert bundle update in their container image.

ben_se: closing notes for POC: root cause = corporate SSL inspection replacing certs; remediation = whitelist POC host or import corp root into runtime. added config snippets for both SDKs to the ticket.

lina_sales: customer happy, asking about permanent solution for production. i'll start convo around Dedicated or Private deployment with their infra team. thanks all!
